claims.text: Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency for determining melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties across large high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.
Integrating high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation can overcome those limitations.
The integrated workflow is applicable to both high-temperature solid and liquid states of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The integrated workflow can operate efficiently over a large compositional space.
Phase composition, crystal structure, and local atomic arrangement mediate the effect of the integrated workflow on prediction quality.
Deformation twinning, FCC-to-HCP transformation, and cross-section reorientation interact synergistically in high-entropy-alloy nanowire deformation.
Local lattice-parameter differences or lattice distortion impede partial-dislocation motion.
The cited deformation and dislocation mechanisms explain how the integrated workflow improves determination of melting and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic-property determinations relative to current methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of melting and liquid-state thermodynamic-property data relative to current methods.
The intervention will improve the efficiency of determining melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys within specific composition and temperature ranges.
Kinetic effects may influence the results of the integrated approach.
